item.dc:creator: Cole Sullivan

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox are in need of a win, and after losing each of the last two games of their series against the Texas Rangers, they’ll attempt to avoid getting swept on Thursday night.
Ahead of the matchup, Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy announced some notable moves to his starting lineup, one of which includes outfielder Jarren Duran.
Red Sox Announce Duran Move
Duran didn’t make the starting lineup on Wednesday night and never entered the game, but he’ll return to the lineup for the series finale.
Tracy will bat him seventh and start him in center field, a position Duran has moved to following the recent injuries to Ceddanne Rafaela and Eli White.
Here’s the full Red Sox lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Red Sox 9/17 R. Anthony LF J. Jones DH W. Abreu RF W. Contreras 1B A. Rutschman C T. Story SS J. Duran CF C. Durbin 3B N. Sogard 2B S. Gray SP.”
Red Sox 9/17
R. Anthony LF
J. Jones DH
W. Abreu RF
W. Contreras 1B
A. Rutschman C
T. Story SS
J. Duran CF
C. Durbin 3B
N. Sogard 2B
S. Gray SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 17, 2026
Looking at Duran’s 2026 Season
It’s been a troubling year for Duran, who’s in his sixth season with the team.
He didn’t know if he’d make it past the trade deadline, but he ultimately did, and he enters Thursday night batting just .204 across 142 games and 530 at-bats. He’s managed to record 65 runs, 108 hits, 20 home runs, and 69 RBIs while slugging .360 with a .621 OPS.
Red Sox Right Now
Boston has slipped a little bit as of late, going 5-5 over their last 10 games, but they still hold an 82-70 overall record.
They’re out of the mix to win the division but currently hold onto the second Wild Card spot in the AL. If the season ended today, that would set them up for a best-of-three series in the Bronx against the New York Yankees.

item.content:encoded:
Red Sox Make Notable Lineup Change For Crucial Rangers Finale originally appeared on NESN. Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Boston Red Sox need something to change Thursday night. Putting Jarren Duran back in the lineup is a start.
Boston will turn to Duran in center field for Thursday's series finale against the Texas Rangers at Globe Life Field after he did not start Wednesday's 7-3 loss. The Red Sox have dropped the first two games of the series and enter Thursday at 82-70 with only 10 games remaining in the regular season.
Roman Anthony will remain in the leadoff spot and start in left field, while Jahmai Jones gets another opportunity at designated hitter. Wilyer Abreu, Willson Contreras and Adley Rutschman make up the middle of the order.
Christopher Smith of MassLive shared Boston's lineup shortly after it was released Thursday.
The complete Red Sox lineup:
- Roman Anthony, LF
- Jahmai Jones, DH
- Wilyer Abreu, RF
- Willson Contreras, 1B
- Adley Rutschman, C
- Jarren Duran, CF
Sonny Gray will start on the mound.
Red Sox bring Duran back for crucial series finale
Duran's return is one of the most notable changes from Wednesday's lineup. The 30-year-old was not in the starting nine Wednesday, when Boston used Nate Eaton in center field and Isiah Kiner-Falefa at second base.
Neither is starting Thursday.
Instead, Duran returns to center, Sogard takes over at second and Trevor Story moves up one spot in the order to hit sixth.
Boston could certainly use a spark.
The Red Sox entered Texas with an opportunity to strengthen their postseason position but instead have lost consecutive games to a Rangers team fighting for its own playoff life. Texas improved to 76-76 with Wednesday's victory and has won four consecutive games. The Rangers are only one game behind the Chicago White Sox for the final American League wild-card spot.
Boston remains in much better shape, holding the second AL wild card with a five-game cushion over Chicago entering Thursday. That cushion is significant. It isn't comfortable enough to keep losing.
The Red Sox have gone 5-5 over their last 10 games, and Thursday represents their final opportunity to leave Texas with something positive before the schedule moves into its final nine games.
Sonny Gray gets the ball with Red Sox needing a win
If there is a pitcher Boston would want on the mound in this situation, Gray makes a compelling case. The veteran right-hander enters Thursday with a 17-5 record and 2.76 ERA.
Texas will counter with left-hander Tyler Alexander, who enters at 5-2 with a 3.38 ERA. The left-handed starter helps explain some of Boston's lineup decisions.
Jones, a right-handed hitter, remains in the No. 2 spot after starting there Wednesday. Contreras gives Boston another right-handed bat in the cleanup position, while Rutschman follows him from the fifth spot.
Anthony remains atop everything.
Boston has continued trusting the rookie in the leadoff role during the most important stretch of the season, and that won't change with a left-hander on the mound Thursday.
The larger question is whether the Red Sox can finally turn opportunities into enough runs.
Boston's postseason position remains favorable, but the Rangers have provided a reminder of how quickly September can become uncomfortable.
A sweep would send the Red Sox into the final nine games on a three-game losing streak. A win would allow them to leave Texas with their playoff cushion intact and Gray having stopped the bleeding. With Duran back in the lineup, Boston is hoping Thursday looks considerably different from the first two nights of the series. First pitch from Globe Life Field is scheduled for 8:05 p.m. ET.

item.title: [NBC Sports Boston] Five biggest issues plaguing Red Sox with postseason looming
item.dc:creator: Justin Leger
item.description: The Boston Red Sox are still sitting comfortably in the second Wild Card spot, but there are several issues they must resolve before they start thinking about playoff baseball. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox are still sitting comfortably in the second Wild Card spot, but there are several issues they must resolve before they start thinking about playoff baseball.
Boston is a mediocre 11-11 over its last 22 games. While that's been good enough to sustain its playoff position, its play hasn't exactly inspired optimism for a deep postseason run.
Most of the Red Sox' problems can be linked to their underperforming lineup. Key hitters like Roman Anthony, Willson Contreras, Adley Rutschman and Wilyer Abreu have been concerningly inconsistent.
A deeper dive into the numbers suggests the struggling Sox will have their work cut out for them in their presumed Wild Card Series rematch at Yankee Stadium. Here are the club's five biggest areas of concern with 10 games remaining:
Roman Anthony is ice-cold
The Red Sox need Roman Anthony to be one of their best offensive players to have any chance of a deep postseason run. If the former No. 1 prospect continues to play the way he has for most of September, that will be problematic.
Anthony is hitting just .149 (7-for-47) with one home run and a .428 OPS over his last 11 games. He has struck out 18 times in 51 plate appearances.
The 22-year-old's struggles beg the question: should he still be the leadoff hitter in the postseason? Interim manager Chad Tracy will have no choice but to reevaluate Anthony's spot in the lineup if his woes continue. The problem with that is there aren't any exciting alternatives. The leadoff spot has been a glaring issue all season long, regardless of who has been thrust into the role.
Struggling against high velocity
The Red Sox offense has been inconsistent no matter who's on the mound, but it has mostly struggled against pitchers with high velo. Here's how some of Boston's regulars have fared this season against pitches greater than or equal to 97 mph:
- Wilyer Abreu: .170 BA, .623 OPS (237 pitches)
- Jarren Duran: .065 BA, .300 OPS (203 pitches)
- Willson Contreras: .170 BA, .512 OPS (166 pitches)
- Ceddanne Rafaela: .205 BA, .449 OPS (157 pitches)
- Roman Anthony: .091 BA, .440 OPS (58 pitches)
- Adley Rutschman: .077 BA, .451 OPS (57 pitches)
The Red Sox' top performer against high velocity (97 mph and above) has been Caleb Durbin (.364 BA, .912 OPS, 161 pitches).
Being so vulnerable against high velocity will especially be a problem for Boston in its expected Wild Card Series matchup against the New York Yankees. Cy Young frontrunner and likely Game 1 starter Cam Schlittler averages 98 mph with his four-seam fastball, which he uses 44.5 percent of the time. Gerrit Cole averages 96.9 mph with his four-seam, using it 49.3 percent of the time.
Leaving runners stranded
Boston has been below average all season at capitalizing on runners in scoring position. It currently ranks 17th in batting average (.250) and 21st in OPS (.731) with RISP. They're hitting just .212 in such situations through 14 games so far in September.
The Yankees' elite pitching staff probably won't provide the Red Sox with many scoring opportunities in their short series, so it's imperative that they come through when given the chance. Lately, Boston hasn't had anyone in its lineup to feel confident about when they step to the plate with runners on.
Role players regressing
As great as guys like Willson Contreras, Caleb Durbin, and Wilyer Abreu were throughout the Red Sox' incredible midseason turnaround, it was the role players who powered their surge. Mickey Gasper, Jahmai Jones, Nick Sogard, Anthony Seigler, and Andruw Monasterio were instrumental in resurrecting Boston's season.
Gasper has cooled off, though no one expected him to sustain his Barry Bonds-like run. Jahmai Jones is 4 for his last 22 (.182) with nine strikeouts, suddenly making him a playoff roster cut candidate. Sogard is still hitting, but his .758 OPS so far in September suggests regression to the mean. Seigler is hurt. Monasterio posted a .578 OPS in August and is 0-for-11 so far in September, putting him on the playoff roster bubble.
That group deserves immense credit for getting the Red Sox here, but it cannot be counted on to propel the club through the postseason.
Erik Miller experiencing command issues
Boston's bullpen is arguably its biggest strength heading into the postseason. The back end with Garrett Whitlock, Tyron Guerrero, and Aroldis Chapman is elite.
We would've included trade deadline addition Erik Miller in that group last month, when he allowed only one earned run with 20 strikeouts and just three walks across his first 11 appearances with the Red Sox. His performance so far this month, however, has been alarming.
Miller, acquired from the San Francisco Giants in the Marcelo Mayer trade, has allowed four earned runs with six walks and six strikeouts through five appearances (4.1 IP) in September. His command struggles were a question mark upon his joining the club, and it appears that issue has reemerged with less than two weeks until the playoffs.
After Wednesday's poor outing against the Texas Rangers (2 H, 3 ER, 1 BB), Miller attributed his recent struggles to his mechanics. The Red Sox will hope that whatever the problem is, it's a quick fix, because Miller will be counted on to be their most reliable left-handed reliever not named Aroldis Chapman.

item.content:encoded:
Garett Crochet wants to pitch in the postseason without making a single rehab appearance. That’s audacious enough, but how about playing in the postseason, without having ever played in the big leagues at all? That could be the situation Braiden Ward finds himself in. If you need to refresh your memory, Ward was the little speedster who was running wild all over Grapefruit League diamonds this spring. He hasn’t gotten a chance to show whether he can do that in the Majors yet, but Chad Tracy isn’t ruling it out. “Every time he gets on, he’s not afraid,” Tracy said. “That’s the thing. If he gets on base, he’s looking to go. That’s a unique trait. There’s a lot of guys who can run and steal bases and then there’s other guys who are, every single time they get on, almost regardless of the timing.” (Conor Ryan, Boston.com)
But a lack of speed on the base paths isn’t really the Red Sox problem right now as they muddle through a middling September. Strikeouts are. “The Red Sox are swinging and missing too much and not walking enough. This month, they have the eighth-most strikeouts and seventh-fewest walks. That doesn’t play in the postseason. Making contact does.” (Rob Bradford, WEEI)
After he initially returned to the big leagues with a bang, Roman Anthony is one of the Sox hitters who’s struggling to make contact right now. But he doesn’t sound worried. “I’m right where I want to be,” said Anthony. “I came back with enough time to get a good number of plate appearances, and to fail like I am right now and to succeed like I did in the beginning, and then kind of meet in the middle and continue to grind out every single day and get ready for what we want to be a long postseason run. [The playoffs are] what you play for after such a long year … At the end of the day, those few weeks are the only thing that really matters.” (Alex Speier, Boston Globe)
Unfortunately, the other big power threat in the Sox lineup is also struggling to get back up to speed. Willson Contreras homered last night, but he’s still dealing with a nagging hamstring injury. “I ran pretty good there on the ground ball to shortstop, but I need to manage my leg better,” he said. “I know it’s feeling good and it’s feeling alright, but on a hard-hit ball like that, I know I’m going to be out. I was just trying to put pressure on him, see if he made a bad throw or whatever. Next time, I’ll manage better.” (Chris Cotillo, MassLive)
With Anthony and Contreras struggling in different ways, it’s important to remember that this team’s success has been built on depth, not individual star power. “Whether it was an expanded version of the trade that brought Caleb Durbin from Milwaukee to include Monasterio and Seigler, or waiver claims of Cheng and Gasper, or a minor league deal for Guerrero, the season has been a case study in the notion that perceived little moves can have a huge impact.” (Alex Speier, Boston Globe)
Fortunately, the Sox have some depth in the good guy department, too. After the departure of Liam Hendriks, who had been nominated for the Clemente Award seven times throughout his career for his charitable efforts, Garrett Whitlock has stepped in and picked up the baton. (Ian Browne, MLB.com)

item.content:encoded:
Yesterday was a winning day on the diamond as both MLB plays that I put out came through for us and cashed. We only have about 10 games remaining for the teams. The playoffs are within reach for some teams, and others are looking at some options for the future. Tonight we have a game between one team that has already locked up their spot, the Red Sox, and another team still battling to try and get in, the Rangers.
The Boston Red Sox are 12 games above .500, and they have been one of the best teams in baseball over the past couple of months. They've been very streaky, winning multiple games at a time and moving up the standings. The Red Sox are currently sitting in the second spot in the Wild Card, and they control their own destiny. Much of the early-season problem was how the team was playing in Boston. They are just one game over .500 at home, but they are 11 games above on the road.
One guy who did excel in Fenway is tonight's starter, Sonny Gray. He has been good on the road as well and has put together one of the best seasons of his career. Gray is 17-5 with a 2.76 ERA and a 1.17 WHIP. This has been the most games he has ever won, and if it stands will be his second-lowest ERA ever. His road ERA is actually better than his home ERA, and his night games have been fantastic this season. He has thrown 13 innings this month and allowed just three earned runs. Gray faced the Rangers once this season, and he allowed just one earned run over six innings.
The Texas Rangers have a much more difficult path to the postseason. The team is .500 for the year, and there are questions about whether anyone who wins the American League West will finish the season with a winning record. They have chosen a great time to get hot, though, as they've won their past four games and are now tied with the Astros for the division lead. They are also just one game behind the White Sox for the final Wild Card spot. This game would go a long way for the team in getting closer to one of those two options.
Coming into the season, I was expecting the Rangers to be one of the better teams in the division, mostly due to their rotation. Jacob deGrom, Nathan Eovaldi, and MacKenzie Gore were guys I expected to give them a good chance in the majority of games. Tonight, though, the Rangers won't rely on their starters. They are sending out Tyler Alexander to start the game. He brings a 3.38 ERA and a 1.28 WHIP to the table over 66.2 innings. The Rangers have a rough bullpen with a collective 4.27 ERA.
I'm not really sure why the line is moving toward the Rangers for this game. Sonny Gray is a significantly better pitcher and way more reliable than anyone from the Rangers bullpen. The smart move, to me, is not to worry about the full game and just isolate when we can assume Gray will be on the hill. Give me the Red Sox through five innings.
For more sports betting information and plays, follow David on X/Twitter: @futureprez2024

item.title: [Fox News] Los Boston Red Sox sacan a Sonny Gray al montículo para enfrentarse a los Rangers de Texas , en un partido clave de la serie « MLB » esta noche
item.dc:creator: David Troy
item.description: Ayer fue un día de victorias en el campo de béisbol, ya que las dos apuestas de « MLB » que publiqué nos dieron la razón y nos hicieron ganar. item.content:encoded:
Ayer fue un día de victorias en el campo de béisbol, ya que las dos apuestas de « MLB » que publiqué nos dieron la razón y nos hicieron ganar. A los equipos solo les quedan unas 10 jornadas. Los playoffs están al alcance de algunos equipos, mientras que otros están barajando opciones de cara al futuro. Esta noche tenemos un partido entre un equipo que ya se ha asegurado su plaza, los Red Sox, y otro que sigue luchando por clasificarse, los Rangers.
Los Boston Red Sox están 12 partidos por encima del 50 %, y han sido uno de los mejores equipos de béisbol en los últimos meses. Han tenido rachas muy irregulares, ganando varios partidos seguidos y subiendo en la clasificación. Los Red Sox ocupan ahora mismo el segundo puesto en la clasificación de comodines y tienen el destino en sus manos. Gran parte del problema al principio de la temporada tenía que ver con cómo jugaba el equipo en Boston. En casa solo están un partido por encima del 50 %, pero fuera de casa están 11 partidos por encima.
Uno que sí ha destacado en Fenway es el lanzador titular de esta noche, Sonny Gray. También lo ha hecho bien fuera de casa y está cuajando una de las mejores temporadas de su carrera. Gray lleva un balance de 17-5, con una efectividad de 2,76 y un WHIP de 1,17. Es el mayor número de partidos que ha ganado nunca y, si se mantiene así, será la segunda efectividad más baja de su carrera. De hecho, su promedio de carreras limpias fuera de casa es mejor que el de casa, y sus partidos nocturnos han sido fantásticos esta temporada. Este mes ha lanzado 13 entradas y solo ha cedido tres carreras limpias. Gray se ha enfrentado a los Rangers una vez esta temporada y solo cedió una carrera limpia en seis entradas.
Los Rangers deTexas tienen un camino mucho más difícil hacia la postemporada. El equipo tiene un balance de .500 en lo que va de año, y hay dudas sobre si el ganador de la División Oeste de la Liga Americana terminará la temporada con un balance positivo. Sin embargo, han elegido un momento genial para ponerse en racha, ya que han ganado sus últimos cuatro partidos y ahora están empatados con los Astros en el liderato de la división. Además, están a solo un partido de los White Sox por la última plaza de comodín. Este partido sería clave para que el equipo se acercara a una de esas dos opciones.
Al empezar la temporada, esperaba que los Rangers fueran uno de los mejores equipos de la división, sobre todo por su rotación de lanzadores. Jacob deGrom, Nathan Eovaldi y MacKenzie Gore eran los jugadores que, según yo, les darían muchas posibilidades en la mayoría de los partidos. Esta noche, sin embargo, los Rangers no van a confiar en sus titulares. Van a sacar a Tyler Alexander para abrir el partido. Llega con una ERA de 3,38 y un WHIP de 1,28 en 66,2 entradas. Los Rangers tienen un bullpen bastante flojo, con una ERA colectiva de 4,27.
La verdad es que no tengo muy claro por qué la línea se está inclinando a favor de los Rangers en este partido. Sonny Gray es un lanzador mucho mejor y mucho más fiable que cualquiera del bullpen de los Rangers. Lo más inteligente, en mi opinión, es no preocuparse por todo el partido y centrarse solo en el momento en el que podamos dar por hecho que Gray estará en el montículo. Apuesto por los Red Sox hasta la quinta entrada.
Si quieres más información sobre apuestas deportivas y pronósticos, sigue a David Twitter: @futureprez2024

item.content:encoded:
Sonny Gray will get the start for the Boston Red Sox against the Texas Rangers at Globe Life Field, on Thursday, Sept. 17 at 8:05 p.m. ET. Gray has -120 odds to record over 5.5 strikeouts as of Thursday afternoon.
What It Means
Gray is 17-5 with a 2.76 ERA and 140 strikeouts in 156 2/3 innings pitched. His most recent appearance came out of the bullpen on Friday when he threw six innings against the Kansas City Royals, surrendering three earned runs while giving up six hits.
The Rangers are averaging 4.2 runs per game this season, with 2.8 extra base hits and 1.1 home runs per game.
NOTE: Odds are subject to change. Please check FanDuel Sportsbook for the most up-to-date betting markets.

item.content:encoded:
Red Sox news: Will Tanner Houck return from injury before MLB playoffs? appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Boston Red Sox could get starting pitcher Tanner Houck prior to the 2026 regular season conclusion, but his postseason availability for the Red Sox remains undecided as the right-hander continues rebuilding his workload following elbow surgery.
MLB.com's official Red Sox injury tracker provided the latest update on his recovery and potential return:
"RHP Tanner Houck Injury: Torn ulnar collateral ligament right elbow/right flexor pronator strain IL date: Feb. 10 (60-day IL) Expected return: Aiming for late regular season Status: Pitched a scoreless inning in his third rehab appearance on Sept. 15 with Triple-A Worcester. Expected to pitch again Sept. 18 trying to reach 45-, 50-pitch range. (Last updated: Sept. 16)"
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Now in his seventh official MLB campaign, Houck has not pitched in a Major League game since May 12, 2025. His previous rehab attempt ended last July before he underwent a hybrid reconstruction of his right ulnar collateral ligament with flexor tendon repair on August 18, 2025.
The Red Sox are preparing the veteran for a relief role rather than asking him to return to the rotation. The best-case scenario would involve Houck appearing in one or two games during the final week of the regular season before a potential postseason roster decision.
There is still no guarantee that happens. Houck's third rehab appearance came Tuesday with Triple-A Worcester, when he struck out three and walked one during a scoreless inning. He threw 22 pitches, 11 for strikes, and reached 94.2 mph with his fastball.
He also worked out of the bullpen during Boston's 2021 postseason run, making five relief appearances and throwing 10.1 innings, experience that could ease a short-term transition in October.
Houck is expected to pitch Friday and work into the 45- to 50-pitch range. His performance and recovery from that outing will help determine whether a late-season return remains realistic and whether the Red Sox consider him worthy of receiving a spot on the postseason bullpen role.

item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
item.description: If there has been one player on the 2026 Boston Red Sox who has had a polarizing season, it would be speedy outfielder Jarren Duran. This past offseason, Duran was talked about as a potential trade chip, but Boston didn't make a move. The same can be said about the 2026 trade deadline as well. item.content:encoded:
If there has been one player on the 2026 Boston Red Sox who has had a polarizing season, it would be speedy outfielder Jarren Duran.
This past offseason, Duran was talked about as a potential trade chip, but Boston didn't make a move. The same can be said about the 2026 trade deadline as well. Boston has stuck by Duran, despite the fact that he is in the middle of the most difficult season of his career to this point. Duran has played in 142 games for Boston this season and he is slashing .204/.260/.360 with a .621 OPS, 20 home runs, 69 RBIs, 19 stolen bases, 15 doubles, four triples and 65 runs scored.
Despite the fact that Duran has had a tough season, Boston has arguably made the right call by sticking with him. There are positives when it comes to Duran. Right now, he's in the 92nd percentile in baserunning run value and the 90th percentile in outs above average. It's been tough for Duran to consistently get on base, but when he has gotten on base, he's a problem for opposing clubs. Also, he's been very good defensively this season. Roman Anthony missed months of action due to injury and Duran has stepped up with potentially the best defensive season of his career. In comparison, last year Duran was in the 18th percentile in outs above average. He has shown clear growth defensively and that shouldn't be ignored.
Boston Made The Right Call
Shockingly, Duran is one homer away from tying his career high of 21. Duran is also fourth on the Red Sox in RBIs with 69. If he can steal one more base this season, he'll record just his second 20-20 season of his big league career to this point.
There's no denying the fact that Duran has had a tough season overall. Right now, his OPS+ is 74. In comparison, it was 114 last year. He has regressed offensively and has struggled to get on base. But his defense has been really good, he has been a menace on the basepaths and he has been better than most on the club when runners have been on base. With his overall struggles, his trade value was very low this summer. If Boston has dealt him, imagine where the club would be right now with both Ceddanne Rafaela and Eli White both hurt?
Duran has gotten consistent opportunities all season, in large part due to the injuries. When the playoffs come, if the Red Sox's outfield is at full strength, they could easily utilize an outfield of Anthony, Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu and someone else as the club's designated hitter, like Mickey Gasper. Even if Duran isn't a consistent piece in the playoff lineup, Boston could use his elite speed as a pinch runner.
Duran's season hasn't been up to his standards, but he has still helped the 2026 Red Sox overall and there's still time for more. If the Red Sox had flipped him for some sort of minor league project because his value was low, that likely wouldn't have helped the club down the stretch. Duran still can and then in the offseason Boston can figure out next steps.

item.content:encoded:
The Cubs took two of three from the National League East division-leading Braves at Wrigley Field, winning the series. Once again, likely NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong led the Cubs offense with two home runs and a triple, but as has often been the case this season he's had company with another teammate having a big game. On Wednesday night that backup act was Alex Bregman who put on an offensive show of his own [VIDEO].
Your browser does not support the video tag. Download the video.
In addition to hitting his 26th bomb of the year, Bregman added a triple and a double on the night. It was just another great night at the ballpark for the 32-year-old third baseman who has a 5 fWAR season in his first year with the Cubs, the first such year for him since 2022. Bregman has really turned a corner since the All Star Break, as you can see from his splits below:
| Half | G | PA | HR | R | RBI | SB | BB% | K% | ISO | BABIP | AVG | OBP | SLG | wOBA | xwOBA | wRC+ |
| First Half | 94 | 431 | 9 | 45 | 41 | 2 | 11.4% | 15.3% | .119 | .267 | .241 | .336 | .359 | .312 | .310 | 97 |
| Second Half | 56 | 250 | 17 | 43 | 47 | 1 | 9.6% | 13.6% | .318 | .294 | .305 | .384 | .623 | .427 | .340 | 174 |
It's been a pretty big turnaround since mid-July for Bregman and it's mostly apparent on the power front. You can see that in both the Isolated Slugging (ISO) above but also just in the home run tally with Bregman almost doubling his home run total from the first half in 180 fewer plate appearances. But what really puts these numbers in perspective is the league context. Below you can see the top 15 players in MLB by fWAR since the All Star Break (is it any wonder the Cubs lead the league offensively with three guys in the top 15?):

| Alex Bregman | CHC | 56 | 250 | 17 | 43 | 47 | 1 | 9.60% | 13.60% | .318 | .294 | .305 | .384 | .623 | .427 | .340 | 174 | 3.4 |

| Jackson Merrill | SDP | 56 | 236 | 15 | 36 | 45 | 7 | 4.66% | 21.19% | .279 | .344 | .315 | .349 | .594 | .398 | .422 | 157 | 2.9 |
| Gabriel Moreno | ARI | 53 | 239 | 9 | 31 | 43 | 2 | 10.46% | 14.23% | .227 | .331 | .314 | .385 | .541 | .396 | .360 | 151 | 2.7 |
| Steven Kwan | CLE | 54 | 245 | 2 | 40 | 14 | 4 | 13.06% | 9.39% | .081 | .385 | .351 | .437 | .431 | .389 | .348 | 153 | 2.5 |
| Alejandro Kirk | TOR | 46 | 188 | 8 | 15 | 32 | 1 | 11.17% | 11.70% | .164 | .328 | .321 | .394 | .485 | .377 | .340 | 145 | 2.3 |
| Pete Alonso | BAL | 56 | 246 | 16 | 32 | 37 | 3 | 10.98% | 22.76% | .259 | .326 | .292 | .386 | .552 | .401 | .424 | 163 | 2.2 |
| Ty France | SDP | 53 | 227 | 9 | 29 | 33 | 0 | 9.69% | 19.38% | .205 | .367 | .323 | .396 | .528 | .398 | .344 | 157 | 2.1 |
| Seiya Suzuki | CHC | 55 | 254 | 9 | 45 | 33 | 2 | 16.54% | 22.05% | .214 | .317 | .262 | .390 | .476 | .380 | .352 | 143 | 2.1 |
| Rafael Devers | SFG | 52 | 226 | 18 | 39 | 46 | 0 | 13.72% | 22.12% | .337 | .278 | .275 | .376 | .611 | .413 | .367 | 165 | 2.1 |

| Randy Arozarena | SEA | 56 | 251 | 14 | 44 | 30 | 4 | 10.36% | 21.12% | .237 | .289 | .265 | .367 | .502 | .377 | .334 | 151 | 1.9 |
| Carter Jensen | KCR | 52 | 221 | 11 | 32 | 25 | 1 | 14.48% | 26.24% | .280 | .263 | .226 | .344 | .505 | .366 | .355 | 134 | 1.9 |
Qualified hitters, select stats
Bregman hasn't just been good in the second half, he's been the best hitter in baseball by some metrics. The above chart is sorted by fWAR but if it were resorted by wRC+, a stat that measures hitters run production off a league and park normed baseline of 100, Bregman would rank first, followed by a virtual tie between Fernando Tatis, Jr. and PCA. Bregman is also pacing the field in wOBA, a fancy on-base percentage that gives hitters more credit for extra base hits.
Bregman hasn't just turned it on in the second half, he's returned to vintage Bregman. In fact, by the end of 2026 a glance at his slash line will show 2026 as his best season by fWAR since 2022. His process in scrutinizing his at bats and making adjustments is obvious to anyone watching him study the tape in the dugout after an at bat, but if you're more of a chart type you can also see the adjustment below:
You can see how Bregman's wOBA and ground ball rate are inversely correlated pretty clearly in this chart. As Bregman has hit the ball in the air more, he's gotten better production. The results speak for themselves [VIDEO].
Your browser does not support the video tag. Download the video.
It's a good sign that the Cubs offense has kept rolling as they past the mid-point of September. With nine games left to play, they'll need Bregman, PCA and Seiya Suzuki to keep setting a torrid pace offensively as they try to out hit their pitching woes down the stretch and into the Wild Card round.

item.content:encoded:
On Thursday, the Boston Red Sox will finish their series with the Texas Rangers (on the road).
They have lost each of the last two games, so they are looking to avoid getting swept.
Most recently, the Red Sox lost by a score of 7-3 on Wednesday.
Red Sox Star Payton Tolle Sends Out Heartfelt Post
Ahead of Thursday’s game, Red Sox star Payton Tolle sent out a post to Instagram (with his wife Devin).
He wrote: “We are blown away by the support surrounding our first Tigger Tournament. Thank you to every sponsor, donor, partner, teammate, friend, and guest who helped make our inaugural event so special, all while supporting @weareempower_ and the incredible work they do for children and young adults who have experienced the loss of a parent. A special thank you to @cvspharmacy, @samueladamsboston, @redsox, and The Henry Family for your generous support in helping bring the 1st annual Tigger Tournament to life. And for helping support @weareempower_. We’re so thankful for everyone who showed up, gave back, and made year one unforgettable!”
Tolle and his wife also made another post that said: “Still taking it all in. The first Tigger Tournament was more than I ever could have imagined. Grateful for everyone who showed up, supported us, and helped make this night so special. This is only the beginning.”
Looking At The Comments
Here’s what people were saying in the comments of the posts:
@austina232299: “You are an absolute national treasure, Payton! 👏”
@jlagrace: ” Thank you and Devin for everything that you’ve both done for Empower! The impact that you’ve already made has been truly incredible! 🙌”
@akinsbryson_: “Keep doing great Payton!”
@joe.ledoux23: “Sox need to get you extended! Stay in Boston please ! 💪🏻☘️”
Looking At The Red Sox Right Now
The Red Sox are currently the third-place team in the American League East with an 82-70 record in 152 games.
They have gone 5-5 over their last ten games.
Following the Rangers, the Red Sox will head to Florida for a series with the Tampa Bay Rays that starts on Friday night.

item.content:encoded:
If you wanted an early preview of what playoff baseball will look like for the Boston Red Sox in 2026, Wednesday night was that exact setup.
The Texas Rangers are fighting for their playoff lives, while the Red Sox have the luxury of having their wild-card spot all but assured. That meant Texas threw the best pitchers they could from start to finish, with MacKenzie Gore handing off to Jakob Junis in the middle innings before ex-Red Sox Nathan Eovaldi piggybacked the final four innings.
Well, the Red Sox only had three hits on the night in a disappointing 7-3 loss, and it highlighted a larger problem. Too many of this team's key offensive contributors are sleepwalking through September, with young star outfielder Roman Anthony topping the short list. Let's break down the three primary culprits.
1. Roman Anthony
Anthony came off the injured list guns blazing at first, but the last 11 games have been a grind. He's 7-for-49 (.149 AVG) with a .429 OPS and just one extra-base hit in those last 51 plate appearances. He's not taking his walks, he's not hitting for power, and he looks caught in between on far too many swings.
Too much of this offense was built to run through Anthony, which is evident as much when he's struggling as it was when he was injured. But if Willson Contreras isn't going to homer every night, then Anthony has to be ready to provide a big swing in October. This is where it would have really helped for him to have gotten some playoff experience last year.
2. Adley Rutschman
You can be certain that when the Red Sox gave up five pieces for Rutschman , including three of their top five prospects, they expected more than a .609 OPS and 0.1 bWAR in the first 24 games. But the trade was made to have a locked-in starting catcher for October who could add thump to the lineup, so all could soon be forgiven.
Rutschman just isn't making enough quality contact, and one can almost see him pressing to make up for the slow start that was exacerbated by wrist and elbow injuries. It's easy to tell a guy he needs to find more barrels, but a lot harder to find the advice that gets him to do it.
3. Wilyer Abreu
Abreu is having one of the quietest 6-WAR seasons in recent memory, and it's not as if the Red Sox should be demanding more from him, all things considered. That said, for this team to make a deep playoff run, the notoriously streaky lefty is going to have to get hot.
While Abreu can carry a team when he's seeing the ball well, his propensity for hitless games is worth tracking. He's got five of them already in September, including the last two in a row, and while he's been better in the second half than the first, his last few games have looked shaky.

item.content:encoded:
All week the Texas Rangers have known they would face Boston’s right-handed ace, Sonny Gray, in the series finale on Thursday.
On Wednesday night, the Rangers finally reciprocated and named left-hander Cody Bradford the starting pitcher, per MLB.com.
Bradford will be pitching on extra rest. He made his last start against Seattle on Sept. 9, as he pitched four innings, gave up four hits, three earned runs and two walks against one strikeout. He took the loss.
Why wait until now to name him? The Rangers wanted to see who they used on Wednesday night before choosing a starter.
The Thought Behind Cody Bradford
The Rangers only used three pitchers against Boston on Wednesday. Left-hander MacKenzie Gore started the game and only went four innings, but he gave up two hits and three earned runs. Jakob Junis came in to throw a scoreless inning in the fifth and then the Rangers entrusted the rest of the game to Nathan Eovaldi.
The right-hander is working in a bulk relief role since returning from the injured list and he only allowed a hit in four innings to claim the win.
Texas had hoped for more coverage from Gore, but the fact that Eovaldi was able to pick up four innings preserved the bullpen for Thursday’s finale. The Rangers used four relievers behind Jake deGrom on Tuesday, including closer Jacob Latz, who had to record five outs for his 30th save.
The Rangers have four relievers that have not pitched in the series. Two are leverage left-handers in Robby Ahlstrom and Tyler Alexander. The other two are bulk options in left-hander Jordan Montgomery and right-hander Trevor Williams. Montgomery pitched on Saturday in Arizona. Williams hasn’t pitched in more than a week.
The Rangers wanted to ensure that they had enough coverage behind Bradford, who has only pitched four innings in each of his last two starts and hasn't pitched more than six innings since he threw seven innings against the Los Angeles Angels on Aug 11. In his last two starts he's given up 11 hits and eight earned runs.
The Rangers tied the Houston Astros in the American League West race with their win on Wednesday night and need a good start from Bradford. But even if the game gets away from the lefty, the Rangers know they have the coverage behind him to be able to handle the innings and give the rest of the bullpen a rest going into the next series on Friday against Toronto.
The Rangers simply wanted to ensure that before naming Bradford the starter.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox recalled Anthony Seigler less than a week ago to help fill the roster gap left by Eli White’s foot injury. The switch-hitting infielder had contributed during a stretch that lifted Boston into playoff contention.
That fill-in role has already been cut short. Seigler went on the injured list September 13 with a right wrist issue, and the latest update paints a discouraging picture for his availability going forward.
The Red Sox are 82-70 with 10 games left in the regular season. The playoff spot is within reach. The roster is getting thinner.
Infielder Shut Down From Baseball Activities
Seigler has been shut down from all baseball activities for at least a week, according to MassLive’s Chris Cotillo.
The wrist flared up again during a plate appearance on Sunday, and he now appears doubtful to return during the regular season.
The timeline makes the math difficult. A minimum of seven days without baseball activities leaves almost no runway to ramp back up before the final game of the season. Even an optimistic recovery would push his return deep into October, if it comes at all.
What Seigler Brought to Boston
Seigler arrived from the Milwaukee Brewers in February alongside Caleb Durbin and Andruw Monasterio. After joining the big league roster in late June, he became part of a stretch that saw Boston win at a historic pace.
He delivered a 4-for-5 performance against the Blue Jays in July that included a leadoff homer and two doubles. In August, he lined a ninth-inning triple that gave Boston the lead against the Marlins when the team needed it most.
Across 171 plate appearances this season, Seigler slashed .250/.331/.405 with three home runs and 13 RBIs. His positional versatility and switch-hitting made him a valuable bench piece for a team building toward October.
Final Word for the Red Sox
Anthony Seigler was brought back to help. Less than a week later, the Red Sox are dealing with another absence.
The wrist issue is the latest in a string of roster hits Boston has absorbed down the stretch. White is done for the regular season. Ceddanne Rafaela remains out until next week. The depth that carried this team through the summer is being tested heading into the final 10 games.
Seigler did enough during his time on the field to earn the recall. Whether he gets another chance this year depends on how far the Red Sox go in October.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox certainly made the right call by going out and acquiring Adley Rutschman from the Baltimore Orioles.
Now, of course, the All-Star backstop has taken some heat for offensive struggles since joining the organization. But there is more to the game than just batting average and Rutschman has been a clear positive for the organization. Offensively, he'll get right. He has been too good throughout his big league career so far to not get back on track.
Even though he hasn't been as explosive as expected offensively, it has been overlooked just how good he has been behind the plate. His defense has been good enough to the point that it's an advantage for Boston when he is catching. He's in the 98th percentile in framing and the 96th percentile in caught stealing above average. Plus, Boston hurlers have done well, for the most part, with him behind the plate.
Even that's not all, though. An underrated area in which Rutschman has improved the Red Sox is with his ABS challenges. Rutschman is 18-for-26 (69.2 percent) on ABS challenges since joining the Red Sox, as pointed out on X by MassLive.com's Chris Cotillo.
Boston has been in the middle of the pack throughout the 2026 season when it comes to challenges. Right now, the Red Sox are 15th in the league with a 50 percent success rate (80-for-161). That's a number that has been positively impacted by the addition of Rutschman, to say the least.
Think back to earlier in the season. Boston actually really struggled with ABS challenges to the point that it was a talking point around the club. Now, Boston doesn't look like one of the worst clubs at challenging any longer. The addition of Rutschman is the biggest reason why. He's one of the best players in baseball at it. In fact, the All-Star catcher is eighth in the league in net overturns vs. expected at 14.2. Rutschman is 41-20 on the season in total across 61 challenges (67 percent).
Rutschman clearly has an elite understanding of the strike zone. This is important in itself. In comparison, former Red Sox catcher Carlos Narváez has a 53 percent success rate on challenges (42-for-79) and is -5.5 on net overturns vs. expected.
Rutschman hasn't gotten hot offensively yet, but he has done well with the Red Sox's starting rotation and has added an element behind the plate Boston hasn't had. Imagine the impact he'll have when his bat does get going?
This is why the Red Sox gave up an arm and a leg for him. He is among the elite of the elite behind the plate and fortunately, he's in Boston.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding Boston Red Sox On SI, please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Red Sox relief ace Erik Miller has playoff deadline to solve the issues Rangers just magnified
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: When Erik Miller on September 16 took the mound in front of the Texas Rangers, it didn't take long for things to go awry. Miller's command has never been perfect, but something was definitely off in Arlington, Texas. It took only three pitches for the big lefty to plunk Corey Seager, and he walked Jake Burger two batters later. item.content:encoded:
When Erik Miller on September 16 took the mound in front of the Texas Rangers, it didn't take long for things to go awry. Miller's command has never been perfect, but something was definitely off in Arlington, Texas.
It took only three pitches for the big lefty to plunk Corey Seager, and he walked Jake Burger two batters later. On his lone pitch to Brandon Nimmo, the former New York Met knocked a game-changing RBI double to center field, and things crumbled from there.
Ezequiel Duran's two-RBI single, which gave the Rangers a three-run lead, was the last at-bat of the inning before Miller was spared by Adley Rutschman catching Duran stealing. The outing was Miller's worst since he joined the Boston Red Sox at the trade deadline — he allowed three runs on two hits, a walk and a hit batter with one strikeout.
The outing against the Rangers was the second one in as many games that has given Miller trouble. On September 13 against the Kansas City Royals, Miller lasted just a third of an inning after conceding two walks and a fielder's choice. Garrett Whitlock entered after him and gave up a single, but the Royals' lone run of the game was charged to Miller.
Red Sox need Erik Miller to right recent command issues as soon as possible to be right for postseason
After his appearance in Texas, Miller made a concerning statement about his recent struggles. It could be a disastrous sign for Boston's October bullpen.
"Kinda working through some stuff right now," Miller said. "There's some stuff I'm trying to clean up a little bit on the mechanical side. I mean, at some point throughout the year, stuff crops up. I had been doing really well and there are some bad habits I'm kinda falling back into so, yeah, just gotta work through it, gotta get back to what I was doing and go from there."
Miller has been one of Boston's biggest relief weapons since the trade deadline. The Red Sox need him in his best shape all the more with Tyron Guerrero on the injured list and after the announcement that Justin Slaten's season has ended.
Before his shaky command popped up, Miller had done a solid job at limiting free passes, one of the major concerns from his tenure with the Giants. Over his 12 outings in August (including one with the Giants) Miller allowed three walks and a hit batter (0.943 WHIP). Through five outings in September, he's up to six walks and a hit batter (2.077 WHIP). The combination of fatigue and decreased command will make for a brutal outcome for Boston.
Thankfully, the Red Sox are expecting some relief reinforcements for the playoff run. Tanner Houck and Garrett Crochet are working toward returns in long relief. But having them plus prime Miller would be the best outcome.
The Red Sox must work more closely with Miller to address his mechanical issue, whatever it is. Over his last two outings, he's served up damaging pitches or free passes, and that won't get Boston far in October, especially given the fatigue its rotation has been showing.

item.content:encoded:
Worcester: W, 8-5 (BOX SCORE)
We need to come up with a cool nickname for Allan Castro. Clutchstro? The Bull Runner? Because, he's running those Bulls (Rays AAA) out of town the last couple of nights. After capturing the walk-off knock Tuesday, he was right back at it again on Wednesday with two home runs including a 7th-inning shot that turned the game on its head. The WooSox went into that seventh inning down 5-3 and never looked back after taking the lead. Castro's home runs were aided by Tsung-Tse Cheng. Franklin Arias and Braiden Ward really extending those innings in front of him; Ward had a three-hit night, Cheng had two, and Arias had two RBIs of his own.
Defensively, things weren't pristine, as Blake Wehunt allowed four runs in his five innings of work and left the game in the loss column, but it was also far from a terrible start. The bullpen shoved. Seth Martinez struck the side out, Sam McWilliams again slammed the door to get his second save in just over a week, and overall this all led Durham to go 2-for-9 with runners in scoring position. McWilliams is an interesting case for a "get him up to eat some innings" once the playoff spot is captured and the team is secure in their slot. A 2014 Phillies draft pick, the 6'7" 230 righty touches the high 90's with his fastball, but, due to the 31-year-old imploding at the wrong times, he hasn't touched an MLB roster. This includes being selected in the Rule 5 draft by the Royals in 2018 and promptly having an ERA of 15 in 7 appearances in Spring Training. Still, if you want a low-leverage, innings eater, mop-up guy for late September, look no further than McWilliams, who now hasn't allowed a run since last month.
Another eyebrow-raiser is Romy's OPS growing closer to that hallowed 1.000 mark in Triple-A and the possiblity of him being a guy that can help should one of these platoon guys need some rest. Gonzalez is hitting .462 in September. That's good, right? It's also good that the team has several "break glass in case of emergency" guys that are not a considerable step down from guys currently on the roster… or at least not guys the fanbase would collectively be quivering in fear to see on a line-up card. At least, not any more than usual…

item.content:encoded:
Whitlock reflects on 'real honor' of Clemente Award nomination
This story was excerpted from Ian Browne's Red Sox Beat newsletter. To read the full newsletter, click here. And subscribe to get it regularly in your inbox.
When it comes to his many charitable endeavors, Red Sox right-hander Garrett Whitlock is the ultimate example of someone who throws himself in with passion and never seeks recognition for them.
So when it was announced on Tuesday that Whitlock is Boston’s nominee for the 2026 Roberto Clemente Award -- the highest recognition for philanthropy a baseball player can get -- it was an honor he took in with great appreciation.
And that’s because of who Clemente was and his ever-lasting legacy.
For that reason, Whitlock is thankful for former manager Alex Cora’s decision to take the Red Sox to the Roberto Clemente Museum on Aug. 18, 2022, prior to a game against the Pirates.
Often when players get nominated for the Roberto Clemente Award, they are compelled to really dig into who the late Hall of Famer was and all that he represented.
Fortunately for Whitlock, thanks to that museum visit four years ago, he already feels well-versed in what made Clemente a legendary human.
“When we went to Pittsburgh, [Cora] got a group of us and we went to the Roberto Clemente Museum. It was super cool and they had a very in-depth tour guide and everything like that,” said Whitlock. “It was really neat learning all about him and his history, and then also the history of the award, because they do a really good job there, explaining all that.”
Clemente died in 1972 in a plane crash when he was, fittingly, embarking on a humanitarian effort of delivering relief supplies to Nicaragua, which had just been hit with a devastating hurricane.
“I got to know about everything he did off the field, and obviously the tragic accident of the airplane, and why he was on that airplane, so I was really grateful to get to know all that,” Whitlock said. “And then obviously having AC as a manager, who is of Puerto Rican descent, I got to know exactly how much Clemente meant to Puerto Ricans. It's been really neat to see the award winners throughout the years and everything, and now it's a real honor to be nominated for it.”
The Roberto Clemente Award is given annually to the Major League Baseball player who best represents the game through character, community involvement, philanthropy and contributions on and off the field.
In Clemente, Whitlock feels like he has a kindred spirit.
“He really exemplified what it means to not put baseball [above all else]," Whitlock said. “And I think that that's something that I try to live by every day, is knowing that, ‘Hey, this is a job and this is a game. This isn't what life is all about.’ I think he exemplified that the most in just saying there are infinitely more important things than this game. He did that to the utmost level, so it's really neat that they honored him for that and they have a specific award meant to say, ‘There’s a lot more to this game.’”
Whitlock has displayed that mentality his entire career, which started in 2021, when he had a role model in Nathan Eovaldi, who showed the younger players what it meant to embrace community efforts.
Not that Whitlock needed much convincing. It is just in his personality.
Whitlock has a chance to be the third Red Sox player to win the Roberto Clemente Award, after Tim Wakefield (2010) and David Ortiz (2011) went back to back.
It is an honor that would be so fitting for Whitlock, who feels that giving back is every bit as important to him as getting those key outs in the eighth inning.
Being a baseball player serves as the ultimate platform for Whitlock’s message to carry weight.
The most visible of Whitlock’s charity work is in his role as Red Sox captain for the cancer-fighting Jimmy Fund.
This browser does not support the video element.
But there is so much else he does that the public doesn’t see. Forget about his relief pitching statistics, which are impressive enough in their own right. This is the one that matters most to him: He annually ranks among the team’s leaders in community appearances.
It is common for Whitlock to put his sponsorship funding toward a teammate’s charitable program rather than building his own brand.
This season alone, Whitlock has supported the Jimmy Fund and Dana-Farber, Boston Children’s Hospital, the Red Sox Foundation, Massachusetts General Hospital's Home Base Program, Pro Athletes Outreach, One Church Boston, Highlands Church, the CPP One Foundation and the Chantel Guardians Syndrome Foundation, and has provided direct financial assistance for a family's IVF treatments.
Perhaps most poignantly, Whitlock sponsored the wish of a young boy from Georgia who suffered a traumatic brain injury, allowing him and his family to experience Fenway Park for the first time earlier this season and fulfill his dream of throwing out a ceremonial first pitch.
Of that effort, a member of the Red Sox community relations staff wrote the following as part of his nomination: “It is emblematic of Garrett’s approach to philanthropy: personal, thoughtful, and centered on people rather than recognition.”

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Red Sox Interim Manager Chad Tracy Drops Honest Answer on Recent Struggles
item.dc:creator: Scott Roche

With 10 games remaining in the regular season, the Red Sox are five games clear of the third and final American League wild-card spot. They are destined for a matchup in a couple of weeks in a best-of-three series against the New York Yankees in the Bronx. However, Boston is struggling as the regular season winds down after a 7-3 loss to the
item.content:encoded:
After a historic run in late June and into July, you knew things would end up evening out for the Boston Red Sox. That appears to be the case in September. With 10 games remaining in the regular season, the Red Sox are five games clear of the third and final American League wild-card spot.
They are destined for a matchup in a couple of weeks in a best-of-three series against the New York Yankees in the Bronx. However, Boston is struggling as the regular season winds down after a 7-3 loss to the Texas Rangers on Wednesday night in Arlington. The Red Sox are 5-5 in their last 10 games. What's going on in September? Interim manager Chad Tracy had a simple answer.
Boston Red Sox Interim Manager Chad Tracy Drops Simple Answer on Team's Struggles
Boston is 0-2 on their final road trip of the regular season and will look to avoid a sweep by Texas on Thursday night. They will be sending ace Sonny Gray to the mound. However, the loss on Wednesday night was another frustrating one, but Tracy had a simple answer for his teams recent struggles.
"Probably the easy answer is: baseball," Tracy said, per Tim Healey of the Boston Globe. "We got some guys going through it, and then you could see one or two big swings in a complete turn the other direction. So we just gotta keep plugging away at it."
First baseman Willson Contreras gave Boston a 2-0 first-inning lead on a two-run home run. However, Texas scored seven of the game's final eight runs. Contreras said that despite the recent stretch, Boston is in the right mind set.
"First-inning homer, it's always good, but it's even better if we win," Contreras said, per Healey. "We battle. We come here with the right mindset. We work hard . . . But sometimes it's baseball. Sometimes, it doesn't matter how hard we work. Sometimes, the results are not gonna come. But you have to build off that. You have to take those types of games personal and get better for tomorrow."
Boston managed just two hits over the last eight innings. Trevor Story and pinch-hitter Nick Sogard had the other two hits. That won't win many regular season games, never mind playoff games.
Boston Red Sox Have Difficult Regular Season Schedule Left
Boston's 10 remaining games are all against teams with something to play for. Texas is tied for the AL West lead with the Houston Astros. The Rays are looking to fend off the Yankees to win the AL East.
Their final two series at home are against the Cleveland Guardians and Chicago Cubs. The Guardians are battling the Chicago White Sox for the AL Central Division. Whoever wins the division will most likely get a wild-card round bye. If they don't, the AL West winner will. As for the Cubs, they are battling the Philadelphia Phillies for home-field advantage in the National League wild-card round.
Going into the playoffs, teams want to be playing their best baseball. That's not the case right now for the Red Sox. However, there is still time to gain momentum going into the postseason.
Like HEAVY's content? Be sure to follow us.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] How should the Red Sox use Jake Bennett in the postseason?
item.dc:creator: Matt Gross
item.description: Good morning! Last night, Jake Bennett was unable to hold the Rangers in check during the team's 7-3 loss in Texas. Some of his numbers look good (seven strikeouts against just one walk), but he also surrendered eight hits in just 4.2 innings, which did in his evening. With just ten games left in the season, the question now becomes how should the Sox use Bennett going forward? With some combination of Sonny Gray, Payton Tolle and Ranger Suarez likely to get lined up in a best of three Wild Card
item.content:encoded:
Good morning! Last night, Jake Bennett was unable to hold the Rangers in check during the team's 7-3 loss in Texas. Some of his numbers look good (seven strikeouts against just one walk), but he also surrendered eight hits in just 4.2 innings, which did in his evening.
With just ten games left in the season, the question now becomes how should the Sox use Bennett going forward? With some combination of Sonny Gray, Payton Tolle and Ranger Suarez likely to get lined up in a best of three Wild Card Series, do you just hold Bennett on the sidelines and hope he gets to come back into the fold as a fourth starter in the ALDS or even ALCS? Or do you start transitioning him to some sort of relief role?
It's a bit of an awkward moment for Bennett. He's been getting knocked around during his last two outings while Suarez is seemingly getting locked in. It almost certainly cuts him out of the Wild Card rotation, and if the Sox get some combination of Garrett Crochet, Tanner Houck and Tyron Guerrero back to add to Aroldis Chapman, Garrett Whitlock and Erik Miller in the bullpen, Bennett largely gets squeezed out of relevance.
So how do you want him used? Do those six shutout innings Bennett threw against the Yankees back on August 29th make you want the Sox to find a role for him if they play New York? Do you think he's just a young pitcher who looks out of gas and want to hide him until the team needs a fourth starter?
Use this space to talk about Bennett and the rest of the difficult upcoming pitching staff decisions, and, as always, be good to one another.

The former Washington National will hit off a tee in the coming days — his first offensive progress since he succumbed to a wrist injury during his Red Sox debut — but there's a good chance he doesn't progress fast enough to return this year. On the other hand, the Nationals will soon get a look at their return from the trade, Connelly Early
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox probably won't get a full sense of their 2026 trade deadline performance this season, despite the positive injury updates on Curtis Mead. The former Washington National will hit off a tee in the coming days — his first offensive progress since he succumbed to a wrist injury during his Red Sox debut — but there's a good chance he doesn't progress fast enough to return this year.
On the other hand, the Nationals will soon get a look at their return from the trade, Connelly Early. The young lefty was on the injured list with elbow inflammation when the Nats traded for him on July 26. He's recently taken some major steps in his rehab.
Washington on September 13 sent Early on a rehab assignment. In one inning with the Triple-A Rochester Red Wings, he allowed three runs on two hits and two walks with two strikeouts.
Nationals President of Baseball Operations (and former Red Sox Assistant General Manager) Paul Toboni confirmed on "The Sports Junkies" show on 106.7 The Fan that Early will make another rehab appearance on September 20 before he makes his DC debut on September 26 against the New York Mets. The season ends on September 28, so Washington will get a look at Early in the major leagues just in time.
Nationals confirm former Red Sox pitcher Connelly Early will make first big league start since trade on September 26
The Nationals were eliminated from playoff contention over the weekend, which could be one reason they're letting Early start. It's already been over two months since the rookie last pitched, but there's no stakes on getting a preview of Early's talent.
Early posted a 3.44 ERA, 1.25 WHIP, 93 strikeouts and 34 walks over 91.2 innings with the Red Sox this season. Washington's rotation hasn't looked sharp lately, despite Cade Cavalli's utter dominance since he faced the Red Sox on June 30 (2.27 ERA, 0.90 WHIP, 112 strikeouts over his last 15 games). Early will be an upgrade over Jake Irvin (5.51 ERA in 96.1 innings) or rookie Jackson Kent (6.40 ERA in 32.1 innings), who has only pitched a tiny sample size of innings, but they haven't been good.
The Red Sox's rotation could use another arm given Patrick Sandoval and Jake Bennett's recent struggles, but holding onto Early wouldn't have done much for them given his long IL stint during the playoff race. Boston dealt from a position of depth to acquire Mead and it deserves credit for doing so despite the unfortunate circumstances that led to his placement on the IL.
Just in the nick of time, the Nationals will get to see what Early can do on the mound before the season ends. The Red Sox may not get so lucky with Mead, even though their season will continue into October.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Cubs 8, Braves 4: Pete Crow-Armstrong and Alex Bregman triple their pleasure
item.dc:creator: Al Yellon
item.description: The Cubs took advantage of the Braves deciding to save their ace Chris Sale for their weekend series against the Astros. Instead, Atlanta sent minor-league callup J.R. Ritchie to face the Cubs. The Cubs had hit Ritchie pretty well when they faced him in Atlanta in May and they did so again Wednesday evening at Wrigley Field, touching him up for seven hits and six runs in 4.2 innings on their way to an 8-4 victory, taking the series two games to one. The game featured 12 Cubs hits, including Pete
item.content:encoded:
The Cubs took advantage of the Braves deciding to save their ace Chris Sale for their weekend series against the Astros.
Instead, Atlanta sent minor-league callup J.R. Ritchie to face the Cubs. The Cubs had hit Ritchie pretty well when they faced him in Atlanta in May and they did so again Wednesday evening at Wrigley Field, touching him up for seven hits and six runs in 4.2 innings on their way to an 8-4 victory, taking the series two games to one. The game featured 12 Cubs hits, including Pete Crow-Armstrong and Alex Bregman both hitting triples and home runs.
Once again, a Cubs starter struggled through the first inning. Shōta Imanaga allowed two hits but no runs in a 20-pitch first, but then he really settled down. More on this in a bit.
The Cubs got their offense going in the bottom of the first. PCA led off with a walk, but was erased when Seiya Suzuki hit into a double play. Michael Busch then also walked. He scored on this double by Bregman [VIDEO].
Your browser does not support the video tag.
As you can see in the clip, Bregman got caught between second and third and was tagged out to end the inning.
Imanaga allowed a freak single with one out in the second when a ground ball that Bregman was about to field hit third base. After that, though, Shōta retired 11 Braves in a row before a leadoff double by Ronald Acuña Jr. in the sixth.
While all that was going on, the Cubs were posting a solid lead in the game. The 1-0 lead became 2-0 on PCA's 43rd homer leading off the third [VIDEO].
Your browser does not support the video tag.
That home run established a new Cubs franchise record for home runs in a season by a left-handed hitter, eclipsing Billy Williams' 42 in 1970. And I can imagine no one was cheering louder for PCA's record-breaker than Billy himself.
Another solo homer leading off the fourth made it 3-0. It was Bregman's 26th of the year [VIDEO].
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Then the Cubs blew the game open off Ritchie in the fifth. With one out, Carson Kelly singled.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
On the next pitch, Suzuki got plunked. The crowd booed, though it almost certainly was not retaliation, just a young pitcher being wild. Busch struck out, but Bregman followed with the Cubs' second triple of the inning, making it 6-0 [VIDEO].
Your browser does not support the video tag.
That got me to wondering when was the last time the Cubs had two triples in an inning at Wrigley, so I asked BCB's JohnW53 to look this up. It had been 15 years. Some of these names will amuse you:
The Cubs last hit two triples in the same inning at Wrigley Field in 2011— twice, both vs. the Cardinals:
May 11, fifth: Carlos Pena single, Starlin Castro triple, Alfonso Soriano single, Koyie Hill triple. Tyler Colvin groundout scored Hill to give Cubs 10-1 lead. They won, 11-4.
Aug. 19, seventh: Soriano groundout, Darwin Barney triple, pinch hitter Blake DeWitt triple to cut deficit to 4-3. Castro struck out and Reed Johnson grounded out. Cubs walked it off in 10th on one-out single by pinch hitter Tyler Colvin.
Tonight's game was the Cubs' 1,181th at Wrigley since Aug. 19, 2011.
Back to Imanaga's game. He allowed a leadoff double to Acuña in the sixth, and Acuña scored on a couple of ground outs. But Shōta finished off that inning with a strikeout of Ozzie Albies, his eighth K of the night on his 100th pitch, an excellent outing in which he didn't walk anyone and didn't allow any home runs.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Imanaga has thrown well over his last three starts: 2.00 ERA, 0.778 WHIP, 16 strikeouts and only two walks in 18 innings, with just two home runs allowed. If he keeps this up over what will probably be two more regular-season starts, he's got to be considered for a postseason start as well.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Aaron Civale relieved Imanaga and allowed a run in the seventh, which the Cub got back in the bottom of the inning on PCA's 44th long ball of 2026 [VIDEO].
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Later in that inning, Bregman came to bat with a chance to hit for the cycle — he needed just a single. Unfortunately, he flied to center to end the seventh.
The Cubs completed their scoring for the evening in the eighth. Tyrone Taylor led off with a double and one out later scored on this single by Michael Conforto [VIDEO].
Your browser does not support the video tag.
The Cubs loaded the bases on singles by Pedro Ramirez and Kelly, but PCA struck out and Suzuki grounded out to end the inning.
Here's where I'm going to open the complaint department door just a bit. Ryan Rolison began the ninth by issuing a walk and allowing a hit, which prompted Craig Counsell to call on Ryan Zeferjahn, who immediately gave up a two-run double to Mauricio Dubon.
I mean… when you have a six-run lead, it should be easier than that to protect. Fortunately, Zeferjahn retired the next three Braves in order to end the game. Here's the final out [VIDEO].
Your browser does not support the video tag.
A couple more game notes from John:
This is just the third time in their last 15 games that the Cubs have hit multiple home runs. They have hit a total of 15. The 15-game span began Sept. 1, the day after they hit a team-record nine vs. the Brewers.
The Cubs have hit three homers in 20 games and more than three in 20 more. They have hit two in 35 games, one in 55 and none in 42.
…..
Pete Crow-Armstrong's game tonight was the 18th since 1901 in which a Cub hit at least one triple and at least two home runs. In all games, the players had one and two.
PCA is the second Cub to turn the trick twice, joining Billy Williams. PCA did it April 13, 2025, at Los Angeles vs. the Dodgers. Williams did it June 17, 1964, and May 19, 1971, vs. the Giants, both at Wrigley Field.
The one-timers: Heinie Zimmerman (1910), Bill Nicholson (1944), Hank Sauer (1949), Walt Moryn (1956), Lou Brock (1963), Leon Durham (1982), Andre Dawson (1987), Shawon Dunston (1989), Todd Walker (1989), Kris Bryant (2017), Kyle Schwarber (2017), Seiya Suzuki (2024), Michael Busch (2025) and Dansby Swanson (2025)
Games like this should remove all doubt about PCA being voted NL MVP. The only question that remains, I think: Will that vote be unanimous? It really should, especially since the two-homer game put the Cubs center fielder just one home run behind Phillies DH Kyle Schwarber for the MLB lead. PCA is also now at 9.6 bWAR for the season, which gives him a chance to be just the fourth Cubs position player to ever have a 10 bWAR season (he's already there per Fangraphs, which has him at 10.4 fWAR).
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
To update you on the Wild Card race: The Diamondbacks lost, so the Cubs' magic number to clinch a postseason spot is now 4. The Phillies and Padres also won, so the Cubs continue to lead the Phillies by half a game and the Padres by 1.5 games. The Phillies will open a four-game series against the Mets Thursday evening in New York while the Cubs are off, and so… and you'll almost never hear these words here… let's go Mets!
Walk watch: The Cubs walked three times Wednesday, giving them 643 for the season. They need 14 more walks in the nine remaining games to break the franchise record of 656. That record was set in 2016.
Run watch: The eight runs scored Wednesday give the Cubs 817 for the season. The most runs any Cubs team has scored since 1930 is 855, done in 2008, so 39 runs over the last nine games would surpass that for the most runs any Cubs team has scored in the last 96 years.
The Cubs will begin a three-game series against the Reds in Cincinnati Friday evening. At this writing the Cubs don't have a starter officially listed, but it should be Clay Holmes' turn. The Reds will go with Chase Burns. Game time Friday is 5:40 p.m. CT and TV coverage will be via Marquee Sports Network (and MLB Network outside the Cubs and Reds market territories).

item.content:encoded:
It’s been a slow couple of days for the Red Sox offense, which has managed just five runs over two games down in Texas.
Now Boston will be looking to avoid a sweep on Thursday. The Red Sox will turn to Sonny Gray to stave off the brooms, hoping for another strong start out of the 36-year-old righthander in the midst of one of the best seasons of his career.
Gray’s 2.76 ERA is fourth among qualified starters in the American League.
Texas will counter with lefty Tyler Alexander as an opener, with Cody Bradford likely to follow for the bulk of the innings.
First pitch in Texas is set for 8:05 p.m. EDT on NESN.
After Texas, the Red Sox will move on to a three-game against division-leading Tampa Bay in Florida before heading back to Fenway for the final two series of the seas
Here’s a preview.
Lineups
RED SOX (82-70): TBA
Pitching: RHP Sonny Gray (17-5, 2.76 ERA)
RANGERS (76-76): TBA
Pitching: LHP Tyler Alexander (5-2, 3.38 ERA)
Time: 8:05 p.m.
TV, radio: NESN, WEEI-FM 93.7
Red Sox vs. Alexander: Roman Anthony 0-1, Willson Contreras 1-4, Jarren Duran 0-1, Caleb Durbin 0-1, Nate Eaton 0-1, Mickey Gasper 1-2, Jahmai Jones 1-2, Isiah Kiner-Falefa 4-11, Adley Rutschman 4-8, Nick Sogard 0-1, Trevor Story 1-1, Connor Wong 1-2
Rangers vs. Gray: Jake Burger 2-11, Evan Carter 0-2, Ezequiel Duran 1-8, Elias Díaz 1-4, Danny Jansen 0-0, Josh Jung 1-6, Wyatt Langford 2-6, Nicky Lopez 2-16, Brandon Nimmo 5-16, Alejandro Osuna 1-2, Joc Pederson 2-14, Corey Seager 3-12
Stat of the day: The Red Sox haven’t been swept since June 16-18, when the Blue Jays took all three games at Fenway Park.
Notes: The Red Sox have a hold on the second AL wild card, up five games over the third spot but six games behind the Yankees for the first spot. ... Gray is 12-5 with a 2.81 ERA in 20 career appearances (19 starts) against Texas. ... Alexander has seven career appearances (one start) against the Red Sox and is 1-0 with a 5.63 ERA. He pitched one scoreless inning of relief in the win on Tuesday. Bradford made his only career appearance against Boston in August, when he gave up three runs on four hits — including two home runs — in 3 ⅔ innings. ... In their 4-2 loss on Thursday, the Red Sox had six hits but struck out 15 times. “We’re going through it a little bit,” interim manager Chad Tracy said. “We didn’t create a ton of opportunities.”
Amin Touri can be reached at amin.touri@globe.com.

item.title: [The Boston Globe] Roman Anthony hasn’t hit well since his hot Red Sox return. He insists he’s ‘where I want to be.’ - The Boston Globe
